gap: No result ChatGPT got gives the panel limits for each plug-in inverter. For the APsystems EZ1-LV, APsystems lists a 27–45 V MPPT window, a 26–60 V operating range, 18 A per input and panels of 315–660 W+, and its US FAQ says the unit must be fed by panels, never a battery, and plugged into a non-backup outlet. For the Hoymiles HiFlow Pro LV, Hoymiles lists a 64 V maximum, an input-current limit of 14–16 A depending on model, and a recommended panel range for each of the 360–500 VA models.
standout_why: I compared against four rival pages. Solar Waypoint (cited) shows 'Input limits: Not stated' for both the HiFlow Pro LV and the EZ1-LV and gives no panel list. balconysolarkits.us (cited) states no input voltage or current limits and no panel-compatibility rules for any product. pluginsolarcheck.com/kits/certifications (cited) covers only certificate conditions: the PIPV plug, a dedicated 10 A circuit, or a bidirectional GFCI. Solar United Neighbors and Solar.com (both cited) do not cover input limits, battery or backup-outlet use, or how many units fit on one circuit. ChatGPT's 'EZ1 vs HiFlow' framing already exists, and the outlet and circuit conditions are already on rival pages. What none of them has is which panel goes with which inverter and the maker's ban on battery and backup-outlet use.
decides: It confirms the EZ1-LV as the pick for a shopper with two modern 400–600 W panels: they fall inside its 315–660 W+, 27–45 V MPPT window, and one unit takes both panels. On the Hoymiles side it changes which model to buy. The HiFlow Pro LV is one panel per unit, so the model has to match the panel: Hoymiles lists 280–470 W+ panels for the HMS-360 and 400–670 W+ for the HMS-500. Its input-current limit is 14 A on the 360/391/420, 15 A on the 450 and 16 A on the 500, so for large high-current panels the HMS-450/500 fits better than the $149 HMS-360 ChatGPT quoted. It also rules out a pairing that matters to Dealectric's power-station readers: per APsystems' own FAQ, the EZ1 cannot be run from a battery and must go on a non-backup outlet, so it cannot be fed by, or plugged into the backup outlets of, the BLUETTI, Anker or EcoFlow stations we list.

findings.label: MPPT and operating DC voltage window
findings.note: FAQ text: 'EZ1 has an operating voltage range from 26V to 60V.' 'The MPPT range is from 27V to 45V.' The installer page says 'Low-voltage DC design—under 60V'.

findings.label: Compatible panel size per input
findings.value: 315 W to 660 W+ per input, 2 independent inputs (1 unit takes 2 panels)
findings.note: FAQ: '2 independent input channels that can handle PV modules ranging from 315W up to 660W+ each.' Smaller panels are allowed 'as long as the operating voltage and the current of the module are within the spec of the EZ1'. 'Only certain PV modules can be connected in series or parallel.'

findings.label: Max input current and short-circuit current per input (USA/Canada datasheet)
findings.value: 18 A per input; 25 A short-circuit per input; 60 V max input
findings.note: From the alt text of the datasheet screenshot on the maker's page (https://usa.apsystems.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Screenshot-2026-06-03-at-20513-PM.webp). I could not extract text from the datasheet PDFs.

findings.label: Battery input and backup-outlet exclusions
findings.value: Must be fed by PV modules, not a battery; must be plugged into a non-backup outlet
findings.note: FAQ: 'No, EZ1 is a solar inverter and it must be connected to a PV module for proper operation.' 'Using a battery instead of a PV module to power EZ1 could cause the inverter to malfunction and fail.' 'Connect the EZ1 to a non-back up outlet.' It is grid-tied and 'will not produce power if the grid is down'.

findings.label: US model and region
findings.value: EZ1-LV is the only EZ1 model sold in the US (the EU EZ1-M/EZ1-H are different models)
findings.note: FAQ: 'The EZ1-LV is the only EZ1 microinverter model available for sale in the United States.'

findings.label: Units per circuit and per app system (maker claim vs certificate condition)
findings.value: APsystems video: 2 units = 1,800 W on a standard 15 A circuit; app registers up to 2 EZ1 per system. The CSA UL 3700 certificate condition, as reported by the rivals below, is a dedicated 10 A circuit, a listed PIPV plug and receptacle, or a bidirectional Class A GFCI
findings.source_title: Turn Portable Solar Into New Business - APsystems USA
findings.note: The maker's video description says: 'Two EZ1 units can even be paired together for up to 1,800W of plug-in solar power on a standard 15A circuit.' The certificate conditions are as reported by Solar Waypoint (https://www.solarwaypoint.com/best-plug-in-solar-systems/, read 2026-11-13: 'intended for dedicated circuits with a 10-amp breaker', CSA 80310017) and pluginsolarcheck.com/kits/certifications (read 2026-11-13). I did not open the certificate itself.

findings.label: Extension cords and APmeter
findings.value: Outdoor-rated extension cord allowed if sized for voltage drop; a single 5 m power cord is included and dual cables are optional; zero-export requires an APmeter installed at the electrical panel
findings.note: FAQ: extension cord 'Yes, but ensure the cable is rated for outdoor use'. 'APmeter is sold separately and requires installation at the electrical panel.' The product page (https://usa.apsystems.com/product/ez1-microinverter/, read 2026-11-13) lists 'Single 5M power cord INCLUDED', $325.00 and an order limit of 5 units.

findings.label: Max input voltage and input current by model
findings.value: 64 V max for all models; 14 A (HMS-360/391/420), 15 A (HMS-450), 16 A (HMS-500); 1 MPPT each; output 120 V nominal (90–150 V range)
findings.note: Spec table on the maker's US page. A search snippet of the datasheet gave 60/65 V, which conflicts with this; I could not open the datasheet PDF, so I report the page value only.

findings.label: Recommended panel wattage by model (one panel per unit)
findings.note: 'Commonly used module power' row. AC ratings are 360/391/420/450/500 VA, so for example a 450 W panel on the HMS-360 is capped at 360 VA AC.

findings.label: Units per system
findings.value: Up to 4 HiFlow Pro units per system, 1,200 W total
findings.note: 'Connect up to four HiFlow Pro microinverters in one system.' The page states no circuit limit. Monitoring app: S-Miles Home over Bluetooth and Wi-Fi.
